definitions: the force or action of one object hitting another:
a powerful effect that something, especially something new, has on a situation or person :
to have an influence on something:
the force with which one thing hits another or with which two things hit each other:
the strong effect or influence that something has on a situation or person :
examples: The impact of the crash reduced the car to a third of its original length .
The bullet explodes on impact (= when it hits another object )
The economic impact on the hospitality industry in the city has been huge .
The anti-smoking campaign had had quite an impact on young people .
Hopefully, what we're doing will make an impact.
The new proposals were intended to soften the impact of the reformed tax system .

more often or to a greater degree :
examples: to be increasingly important / common

rather than; as an alternative :

definitions: the quality of being important :
examples: The health report stresses the importance of fresh food in a diet .

importance of The health report stresses the importance of fresh food in a diet .

definitions: a single person or thing, especially when compared to the group or set to which they belong :
a person who thinks or behaves in their own original way:
existing and considered separately from the other things or people in a group :
given to or relating to a single , separate person or thing:
belonging or relating to, or suitable for, people or things that are different or particular in some way:
examples: Every individual has rights which must never be taken away.
Like many creative individuals, she can be very bad-tempered .
We try to treat our students as individuals.
If nothing else , the school will turn her into an individual.
Each individual table is finished by hand .
We deal with each case on an individual basis .

definitions: the ability to learn , understand , and make judgments or have opinions that are based on reason :
secret information about the governments of other countries , especially enemy governments , or a group of people who collect and deal with this information :
the ability to understand and learn well, and to form judgments and opinions based on reason :
a government department or other group that gathers information about other countries or enemies , or the information that is gathered :
the ability to learn and understand things quickly and easily :
examples: an intelligence test
a child of high/ average / low intelligence
It's the intelligence of her writing that impresses me.
the Central Intelligence Agency
military intelligence

definitions: a subject or problem that people are thinking and talking about:
most important in what is being discussed :
to make something seem more important than it should be, or to argue about it:
to disagree strongly :
to dislike or disapprove of someone or something and let it upset or worry you:
examples: environmental / ethical / personal issues

Of course I'll help you - there's no need to make an issue of it.

definitions: the large system of connected computers around the world that allows people to share information and communicate with each other:
the large system of connected computers around the world which people use to communicate with each other:

the fact of the internet being available to use:
relating to the internet:
examples: Use your phone to connect to the internet.
I found out about the bombings on the internet.
Free versions can be downloaded from the internet.
Sorry, I won't have internet access while on holiday .

definitions: the power to have an effect on people or things, or a person or thing that is able to do this:

to cause someone to change a behavior , belief , or opinion , or to cause something to be changed :
the power to have an effect on people or things, or someone or something having such power :
examples: Family is the most important influence on children .

definitions: the feeling of wanting to give your attention to something or of wanting to be involved with and to discover more about something:
Your interests are the activities that you enjoy doing and the subjects that you like to spend time learning about:
the quality that makes you think that something is interesting:
something that brings advantages to or affects someone or something:

definitions: to communicate with someone or react to something:
to react to something on the internet , for example by watching a video , posting a comment (= a reply underneath ) , or liking it (= clicking a symbol to show that you approve ) :
to communicate with or react to each other:
to communicate with someone:
if two substances , areas of business , etc. interact, they work together or have an effect on each another:
examples: Dominique's teacher says that she interacts well with the other children .

definitions: using new methods or ideas :

definitions: used for saying that a person or thing is part of a particular group or amount :

definitions: not simple and therefore difficult to understand :
being in a close relationship with someone:
difficult to understand or deal with; complicated :
interested in something you are doing:

examples: an involved reason / excuse / argument
The plot of the film was too involved - I couldn't understand it.
emotionally / romantically involved
When did you two first become involved?
As a doctor , you should not become too emotionally involved with the children in your care .

definitions: present participle of improve
to ( cause something to) get better :
examples: He did a lot to improve conditions for factory workers .
